forecast.verdict: revise (gate 85; no story.json, scored from script text, peak not scored)

items.note: Thumbnail/cold-open idea is right, but the game is not named until l006 (~35 s). A stranger at 5 s hears 'thirteen years for one video game' with no subject.
GTA 6 launch week is a household topic.

Hotel TV promised at 0:12 (l003), paid at l043 (~3:15 in). Held too long with two stat pieces in between. Title 'almost broke it' overclaims: the leak hurt nothing that the script shows. Prefer 'A Hotel TV Hacked It'.
Piece structure and the but/therefore handoffs (l021, l035, l049, l060, l069, l081) are a real spine. Pieces 1 and 2 are statistics with no mid-payoff; piece 5 is flat.
l094 ('trailers say yes, price says maybe') is a shrug. Skip asking the next question (l097) is right and the hotel TV is recapped in l093.
l098 is a real open fight (worth 80 dollars + 13 years) and 'Tell Skip he is wrong' is woven. l100 score out of 7 is weak: the viewer cannot really 'know' pieces.
Hotel TV hack and the publisher-started panic are retellable. Several fact lines have no visible support (see notes).

caps: none triggered; claims need the fact-checker's evidence before retell is above 3 (cap would apply if l056, l074, l083-l086 fail)

reasons_to_underperform: The first 40 s do not name the game or the hotel-TV payoff location: l001 says 'a video game' and GTA is named at l006; the pieces count arrives at ~50 s, after a 70-word l005/l006 wall.
Pieces 1-2 (about 2.5 minutes) are numbers and nostalgia with no surprise until l043; the TV tease is the only reason to stay and Skip's gag is spent at l002.
Several claims sound unsupported and a few contradict each other (l005 'more than any film' vs l033 'one of the most'); the l083 'on purpose' claim is the second headline and needs a source.

opening.at_5s: ~13 words (l001): somebody waited 13 years for 'a video game'. Does not know which game. Stays only on curiosity.
opening.at_15s: ~38 words (l001-l004): a teenager broke into it from a hotel TV; Skip is skipping then hooked. Stake is clear ('how does a TV break a game?'), game still unnamed. Stays: yes, this is the strongest beat.
opening.at_30s: ~73 words (l001-l005): game still not named, only 'the week it came out the internet fought'. Name arrives in l006 (~35 s), 'seven pieces' list in l007 (~50 s), stamps rule ~57 s. Misses the 30 s 'what you will see' target by ~20 s.
opening.stay_verdict: Likely stays through 15 s (good), leaks between 30 and 55 s unless l005-l006 are cut and the game is named in l001.

gap_to_gate.item: name the game in the first sentence (stop 11/15, 5 s test)
gap_to_gate.now: Thirteen years. That is how long the world waited for one video game.
gap_to_gate.needed: Thirteen years. One game. Grand Theft Auto Six. And a hotel TV nearly broke it.

gap_to_gate.item: cut the 70-word wall so stakes and pieces count land by ~35 s (drive/promise)
gap_to_gate.needed: l005: It may have cost more than any film ever made. It was delayed twice. And launch week, the internet started fighting about it. | l006: This is the story of Grand Theft Auto Six. Waiting, money, and one very bad night for a hotel TV.

gap_to_gate.item: piece 1 needs a small answer (drive, Short ending)
gap_to_gate.needed: Because they did not need to hurry. Piece two shows why.

gap_to_gate.item: Skip must be the smart objector, not naive
gap_to_gate.needed: Nobody is that slow. What were they doing?

gap_to_gate.now: Rockstar, the company behind Grand Theft Auto, released exactly one other big game.
gap_to_gate.needed: Rockstar, the company behind Grand Theft Auto, put out just one other giant new game in those years.

gap_to_gate.item: cut sentimental line, shorten piece 1 sag
gap_to_gate.now: A kid who was ten years old that day is twenty-three now. He finished school. He got a job. He might have a kid of his own.
gap_to_gate.needed: A kid who was ten years old that day is twenty-three now. He finished school and got a job.

gap_to_gate.item: Skip objects instead of asking for an explanation
gap_to_gate.needed: Views are cheap. Is that actually a lot?

gap_to_gate.item: running gag: Skip tries to skip at the slowest moment (piece 5), so 'Do not touch that button' has a cause
gap_to_gate.now: SKIP: Twice? | KARTO: Twice. Do not touch that button. Because every time...
gap_to_gate.needed: SKIP: Twice? Okay, this piece is slow. Skipping. | KARTO: Do not touch that button. Every time this game moved, other companies had to move their own games out of the way.

gap_to_gate.item: shorten legal detail after the peak (keeps momentum, fewer claims)
gap_to_gate.now: The court found that he did it. Doctors said he was not well enough for a normal trial, so the judge sent him to a secure hospital, with no end date.
gap_to_gate.needed: The court found he did it. A judge sent him to a secure hospital, with no end date.

gap_to_gate.now: Every new game since, the same play. Somebody on TV says it will ruin the youth. The youth says: thanks for the advert.
gap_to_gate.needed: Since then, the same fight comes back with every release. Somebody on TV says it will ruin the youth. The youth says: thanks for the advert.

gap_to_gate.now: But here is the secret. This exact fight is as old as the series. And the first time, the game's own publisher started it on purpose.
gap_to_gate.needed: Here is the secret behind every GTA scandal. This fight is as old as the series. And the first time, the game's own publisher started it on purpose.

gap_to_gate.now: So was it worth it? The trailers say yes. The price tag says maybe.
gap_to_gate.needed: So was it worth it? Thirteen years of trailers say yes. Eighty dollars says ask your wallet.

Unsupported-sounding claims for the fact-checker: l005 (more than any film), l015/l018, l019, l024, l025, l028-l030 (twelve years of online spend), l044 (most expensive game in the world), l046 (five million), l047, l053, l055, l056 (475M, company claim), l062, l074 (no 60 fps mode, reports), l077, l082 (unnamed TV host), l083-l086 (publisher started it on purpose, publicist), l090 (scientists), l091 (adults only).
